name: six-face-spaced-run
description: The DEFAULT six-face run, T-019's best-measured reflex policy: six-face-aimed-run.json plus the two clauses this task's per-tick forensics justified. (1) PERSONAL SPACE — step away from the nearest body when it is inside 2.2 tiles, because the shipped policy's most common damage event is walking or hopping into a CRUISING hostile, not being dived on (a low-lane wasp bobs down to 1.7 above its deck, exactly a standing RIG's head). (2) DON'T POGO AGAINST SOMETHING THAT ISN'T A STEP — `pinned` reports 'jammed while trying to run' without saying why, so answering every pin with a jump makes RIG bounce against the screen's own right clamp, which during a gate sits at the corner pivot; `terrain.stepUp>0.5` makes the jump answer an actual step. MEASURED, NOT ASPIRATIONAL (2026-08-01, `main` pinned and served, --deterministic --stop-on-game-over --max-runtime-ms 145000, 1440x900, 7 runs — every one ended at GAME_OVER long before the window): survives 50.2-55.1 s (median 53.6) against the shipped aimed policy's 46.7-52.8 s (median 48.6, 4 runs), 10-16 kills, and reaches wave gate 2 / scroll 140 of 415 EVERY time without clearing it. It does NOT reach VICTORY and no bot run has: the wall, the arithmetic behind it, and the operator packet that has to answer the delivery box are in docs/playtests/2026-08-victory-box.md. Read that before writing another full-run policy. Run-to-run spread is +/-6 s, so read the gate reached, never one run's decimals.
